column3: NASB leaves the sentence open, continuing in verses 2–3.
NASB supplies “part,” “spoils,” and “of his name”; “first being translated” is rendered “first of all, by the translation of his name.”
“Unto all time” is rendered “perpetually,” and NASB adds “but.”
“Consider” is rendered “observe,” and “best spoils” “choicest spoils.”
“Loin” is rendered “descended,” and “brothers” “brethren.”
“Not tracing his ancestry” is rendered “whose genealogy is not traced.”
“Inferior … superior” is rendered “lesser … greater.”
“Here … in that place” is rendered “in this case … in that case”; NASB supplies “one receives them.”
Close to the Greek.
Close to the Greek.
NASB uses parentheses instead of dashes; “to be named” is rendered “be designated.”
Close to the Greek.
“Served” is rendered “officiated.”
NASB follows the critical text (“concerning priests”); “has sprung” is rendered “was descended.”
“More excessive yet evident” is rendered “clearer still.”
“Fleshly commandment” is rendered “physical requirement,” and NASB supplies “such.”
“It is testified” is rendered “it is witnessed of Him.”
“Preceding” is rendered “former”; NASB adds “on the one hand.”
NASB adds parentheses and “on the other hand there is.”
NASB keeps “And inasmuch as it was not without an oath” here and joins “for they indeed became priests without an oath” to verse 21.
NASB follows the critical text, without “according to the order of Melchizedek”; it begins the verse with the parenthesis about the other priests.
“By so much” is rendered “so much the more.”
NASB supplies “former” and renders “many” as “existed in greater numbers.”
Close to the Greek.
“To the uttermost” is rendered “forever,” and “living” “since He always lives.”
NASB supplies “that we should have,” and renders “having become higher than the heavens” as “exalted above the heavens.”
“As the high priests” is rendered “like those high priests”; NASB adds “because.”
“Having weakness” is rendered “who are weak”; NASB supplies “came” and “appoints.”
